facts.text: The study replaced the liquid-phase empirical EAM reference potential used in the original TOR-TILD workflow with a machine-learning moment tensor potential (MTP).
The study replaced the original thermodynamic-integration calculations with free-energy perturbation (FEP) calculations between the MTP and DFT descriptions.
The DFT-based free-energy calculations were performed at 0 GPa using both GGA-PBE and LDA exchange-correlation functionals.
Solid-state short-range order was analyzed over 2000–2400 K.
MTP training and molecular-dynamics sampling used a 12×12×12 supercell containing 3456 atoms.
The trained MTP closely reproduced the ab initio phase-space distribution and achieved training errors below 1 meV/atom.
FEP converged rapidly because the energy differences between the MTP and DFT descriptions had small variance, avoiding the slow convergence of thermodynamic integration.
Electronic Gibbs-energy contributions associated with a density-of-states gap at the Fermi level shifted the calculated melting temperature.
Solid-state short-range order stabilized the solid phase by approximately 2.4 meV/atom, corresponding to an approximately 25 K melting-temperature contribution.
Relative to the original EAM- and thermodynamic-integration-based TOR-TILD method, the MTP-FEP workflow reduced computational resource use by 80%, reported as an approximately 20-fold speedup.
Benchmark FEP free energies agreed with thermodynamic-integration results to within 0.5 meV/atom.
Electronic excitations shifted the melting point by 48 K with GGA-PBE and 57 K with LDA; the resulting melting points were respectively 193 K and 160 K below the extrapolated CALPHAD value.
